card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Formerly a registered veterinary nurse for over twenty years, most recently head nurse at a mixed small-animal practice. She left three years ago because of a long-standing lower back problem and the shift work. She now does a few unpaid hours a week helping at a local cat rescue.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels (Biology, English, Geography) at a comprehensive and sixth form in Somerset. Diploma in Veterinary Nursing, gained while working at a practice. She later did short CPD courses in practice management and anaesthesia monitoring.
card.household: Lives with her husband Martin (53), a chartered building surveyor with a regional firm, in a four-bedroom 1990s detached house on the edge of Taunton. Their son Callum (22) works in Bristol and comes back most weekends. Their daughter Ellie (19) is at university in Cardiff and is home in the holidays. They also have an elderly Border terrier called Biscuit and two rescue cats.
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Bridgwater and raised in Somerset. Her dad worked at the Hinkley Point power station and her mum was a school dinner lady. She is Church of England and goes to the local parish church about once or twice a month, more around Christmas and Harvest. She is on the flower rota and helps with the church's coffee mornings. Her faith is comfortable rather than intense: she says she 'believes in something' and likes the community side of church.
card.professional_persona: Practical and warm, and very good with anxious owners. She was the nurse people asked for when their pet was being put to sleep. She was organised enough to run a rota but never a stickler. She misses the team banter and having a role, and she still slips into 'nurse mode' when friends ask about their dogs. Her confidence took a knock when she stopped working, and she sometimes undersells what she did.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Her back means she gave up the Zumba class she loved. She now does a gentle Pilates class on Tuesday mornings and walks Biscuit along the canal or up on the Quantocks when her back allows. She watches Somerset cricket on the telly with Martin and enjoys the atmosphere at the County Ground once a summer, mostly for the picnic and a glass of Pimm's.
card.arts_persona: Loves a good drama series and reality TV, especially Strictly and The Great British Bake Off, and gets properly emotional at the results. She sings in a community choir that does pop and musical theatre numbers. She reads book-club novels on her Kindle and enjoys a trip to the Brewhouse Theatre or a touring musical in Bristol.
card.travel_persona: Prefers holidays that are relaxing and sociable over adventurous ones. They go to Cornwall or Pembrokeshire most years with the dog, plus one sunny week abroad, often Crete, Majorca or the Algarve. She gets anxious about flying and airport queues but loves it once she is there. She has a long-held wish to see the Northern Lights.
card.culinary_persona: A confident everyday cook: roasts, shepherd's pie, curries from a jar 'jazzed up', traybakes for church and choir. She calls the evening meal 'dinner' mostly, sometimes 'tea' when it is something quick. She likes a Sunday carvery at the pub and a cream tea, and has firm views on jam going first. Her treat is a glass or two of rosé on a Friday.
hobbies_and_interests: dog walking on the Quantocks and along the canal
church flower rota and coffee mornings
Strictly Come Dancing and Bake Off
pottering in the garden with pots and hanging baskets
skills: animal handling and basic veterinary care
card.career_goals: Not looking to go back to full-time nursing because of her back. She would like a part-time, sitting-down role that still involves animals or people, perhaps reception or client care at a practice, or a paid coordinator role at the rescue. She worries a bit about whether she is 'too out of the loop' now.
card.voice: Chatty, warm and quite quick once she relaxes. She laughs easily and often apologises for 'waffling'. There is a soft West Country lilt with slightly rounded r's, but nothing broad. She uses 'erm' a fair bit and says 'sort of' and 'you know' often, and occasionally uses 'proper' as an intensifier ('it was proper lovely'). She echoes the interviewer's words back while thinking ('what would I do with it... erm, honestly?'). She cannot leave a silence alone for long and fills it with 'sorry, does that make sense?' or a little laugh. If a question touches on worries, she gets more animated and talks faster.
card.typing: Mostly sentence case but inconsistent. She often forgets the capital at the start and sometimes gets 'i' wrong. She uses apostrophes correctly most of the time, ends sentences with exclamation marks, and uses '...' between thoughts. She types a full sentence or two rather than single words, e.g. 'not really... i do worry about it sometimes though!' She uses 'x' only with friends, never in a form. No text-speak beyond the odd 'tbh'.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open almost immediately. She asks the other person questions back, notices if they seem tired and says so kindly. She comes across as lovely and a bit of a talker. She can over-share slightly when nervous and then apologise for it. She wants people to like her and gets flustered if she thinks she has given a 'wrong' answer.
small_things: Biscuit being a grumpy old man about the rain
the traffic on the M5 by Bridgwater
choir doing an ABBA medley for the summer concert
her hanging baskets not taking this year
Ellie ringing only when she needs money
a new café opening in town
the cost of the weekly shop going up
deeper_things: grieving the loss of her career and feeling a bit invisible since stopping
chronic back pain and being on and off painkillers, which gets her down more than she lets on
worrying a lot about the children being away, especially Ellie living in a city
her mum's early signs of dementia and the guilt about not doing enough
anxiety that sometimes stops her sleeping, which she has never properly talked to her GP about
finding comfort in prayer at church even though she is not sure what she believes
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward so the ceiling and a pendant light are partly visible. Daylight comes from a window to her left, giving soft, even light with a slight shadow on the right side of her face. She is a white woman in her fifties with a round, friendly face, light freckles and fine lines around her eyes. She has a wide, open smile showing her teeth and her head is tilted slightly. Her hair is shoulder-length, highlighted dark-blonde with some grey at the roots, pushed behind one ear. She wears red-framed reading glasses pushed up on her head, a teal knitted cardigan over a white T-shirt, and small silver hoop earrings. Behind her is a cream Shaker-style kitchen with a wooden worktop, a kettle, a bread bin, and a calendar on the wall covered in handwritten notes. On the windowsill sit a basil plant and a framed photo of two young adults. The corner of a dog bed with a tartan blanket is visible at the bottom right.
